title: Animas River after Gold King
question: After adjusting for discharge and season, did metal concentrations in Cement Creek and the Animas River change in a lasting way after the August 2015 Gold King Mine release, and can any change be told apart from the treatment plant that started two months later?
one_liner: A pre-registered, flow-adjusted interrupted time series on Water Quality Portal and USGS discharge records, with a 27-fit sensitivity grid, a blind change-point search, an upstream control and false-discovery control across every site and metal.

headline.label: Level change at the release, dissolved zinc, Cement Creek
Strongest blind change-point, months from the release
Sensitivity grid fits
headline.note: range of level change from the grid shown below

finding: The headline cell is dissolved zinc in Cement Creek, {{its.headline.n}} monthly samples from one organisation between 2005 and 2025, flow-adjusted with a concentration-discharge regression and seasonal harmonics. With the pre-period starting in 2005, the level change at the release is {{its.headline.level_change_pct:pct_signed}} with a 95 percent interval from {{its.headline.level_change_pct_lo:.0f}} to {{its.headline.level_change_pct_hi:+.0f}} percent and p = {{its.headline.level_change_p:.2f}}. The pre-registered verdict is: {{its.headline.verdict}}.

The verdict depends on the analyst's choices. The pre-period carries a rising trend of {{its.headline.pre_slope_pct_per_yr:.1f}} percent a year that the counterfactual extrapolates; starting it in 2010 or 2013 makes the decrease significant, and ending the post-period in 2016 flips the sign. Across {{grid.n_fits}} fits the level change ranges from {{grid.pct_min:.0f}} to {{grid.pct_max:+.0f}} percent and {{grid.n_ci_excludes_zero}} intervals exclude zero.

A change-point search that does not know the release date puts the strongest split at {{cp.headline.strongest_month}}, {{cp.headline.strongest_rel_release_months}} months from the release. On a series with three coding artefacts removed, the strongest split is {{cp.explore.strongest_month}}, {{cp.explore.strongest_rel_release_months}} months after the release and {{cp.explore.strongest_rel_plant_months}} months after the Gladstone treatment plant started. Across {{mult.n_cells}} site-by-metal-by-fraction cells, {{mult.n_estimable}} are estimable, {{mult.n_raw_sig}} have raw p below 0.05 and {{mult.n_bh_sig}} survive false-discovery control. Pooling the organisations that began sampling after the spill gives {{explore.pooled.level_change_pct:.0f}} percent, double the single-organisation estimate.

traps.how: Pre-period start, post-period end and plume window move the level change from {{grid.pct_min:.0f}} to {{grid.pct_max:+.0f}} percent across {{grid.n_fits}} fits; the primary specification was frozen before fitting.
{{mult.n_raw_sig}} of {{mult.n_estimable}} cells have raw p below 0.05 and none survive Benjamini-Hochberg at 5 percent FDR.

Sampling went from {{coverage.events_per_year_pre:.0f}} to {{coverage.events_per_year_post:.0f}} events a year after the plant started; pooling the new organisations doubles the apparent decrease, so one organisation is held constant across the release.
Non-detects enter a Tobit regression as bounds; 12 cells were ruled not estimable by the pre-registered censoring rule rather than filled.
The upstream control's own change was driven by three zero-coded non-detects; a difference-in-differences against it is reported alongside the single-site estimate.

figures.caption: Level change in flow-adjusted dissolved zinc at Cement Creek under every combination of pre-period start, plume window and post-period end. Starred cells have intervals excluding zero.
The interrupted time series on flow-adjusted residuals, with the release, the treatment-plant start and the extrapolated pre-period trend.
Blind change-points on the cleaned series; the strongest lands after the treatment plant started, not at the release.
Every site, metal and fraction: point estimate, interval, and whether it survives false-discovery control.
Concentration against discharge before and after the release.
Reporting limits over time by organisation and method.

not_claimed: No attribution of any change to the release; the release and the treatment-plant start are two months apart, inside the resolution of a monthly series.
No health, ecological, compliance or legal conclusion.
The cleaned-series result with an interval excluding zero is exploratory, not confirmatory.
